Ripple Meritz Securities: Powerful 4th Deal, Major Win
sum: Ripple Meritz Securities partnership has entered Korea’s capital markets, announced on October 14, to provide institutional custody and tokenization infrastructure. This Ripple Meritz Securities agreement, Ripple’s first with a Korean securities company, will integrate Ripple Custody into Meritz’s current securities operations and prepare for tokenized asset issuance as Korea’s digital asset regulations develop.

It marks the Ripple Meritz Securities deal as Ripple’s fourth significant institutional partnership in Korea in 2026, following deals with Kbank, Jeonbuk Bank, and Kyobo Life Insurance. These partnerships cover banking, insurance, and now brokerage, establishing Ripple Meritz Securities collaboration as part of a comprehensive infrastructure push in one of Asia’s most active digital asset markets.

Ripple Meritz Securities partnership brings together Meritz Securities, part of Meritz Financial Group active in brokerage, investment banking, and asset management. For Ripple, this Ripple Meritz Securities collaboration offers access to securities issuance and distribution channels that retail banks do not provide.

The Meritz agreement completes a targeted vertical strategy. Ripple has worked with Kbank to implement wallet infrastructure through Ripple Custody, with Jeonbuk Bank to update cross-border payments, and with Kyobo Life Insurance to enable Korea’s first tokenized government bond settlement on blockchain.

Each Ripple Meritz Securities-related partnership addresses a separate area: Kbank for neobank custody, Jeonbuk for payments, Kyobo for insurance settlement, and Meritz for capital markets. This is significant because Korean financial groups operate in all four areas, and the Ripple Meritz Securities infrastructure that functions across these sectors is more likely to become an industry standard.

This timing coincides with a major regulatory push by the Financial Services Commission in Korea. In 2026, the FSC has advanced rules for spot crypto ETFs, security token offerings, and KRW-pegged stablecoins and has tightened investor protections under the Act on Protection of Virtual Asset Users.

Bitcoin Price Falls Below $82K as $406M in Longs Get Liquidated
sum: Bitcoin cracked below $82,000 Monday evening, setting off another painful reckoning for leveraged crypto traders. Nearly $489 million in positions vanished over 24 hours, with bullish bets accounting for more than 83% of the damage as the broader market stumbled.
- Bitcoin fell below $82,000 Monday as $488.61 million in crypto liquidations hit 118,142 traders.
- Coinglass data shows bullish positions accounted for $406.48 million, or 83.2%, of liquidations.
- Ethereum, solana and XRP joined bitcoin’s decline as investors awaited Wednesday’s CPI report.

On Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, bitcoin’s price slipped below the $82,000 threshold, extending a decline that had dragged the cryptocurrency down from an earlier high near $84,254. By approximately 7:30 p.m. Eastern time, Coinglass liquidation figures showed $488.61 million in leveraged crypto positions had been wiped out over 24 hours.

The damage reached 118,142 traders, with long positions accounting for $406.48 million and shorts contributing $82.14 million. Put differently, more than $83 of every $100 liquidated came from traders betting on higher prices. Ethereum led individual assets with $115.19 million in liquidations, followed by bitcoin at $106.61 million.

The crypto asset solana (SOL) contributed another $26.97 million, while zcash and NEAR registered approximately $19.86 million and $19.81 million, respectively. Binance accounted for 52.3% of the total. The largest individual liquidation was a $9.65 million bitcoin long position on Binance, executed at $81,772.

items.t: Stock Falls 10%, Analyst Raises Price Target: What Changed at the Tokenization Company?
sum: StoneX raised its price target from $12 to $18, citing the revenue potential of Securitize’s new stock-token platform, as the company’s shares fell 10% Monday morning.
According to The Block, StoneX analyst Mark Palmer maintained his “Buy” rating on Securitize. The new target implies approximately 45% upside from the price Monday morning cited in the report.

At the center of Palmer’s optimism is Securitize Stocks, which launched last Thursday. The analyst argues that the company should now be viewed not only as a service provider that brings assets onto the blockchain, but also as an operator of the market where those assets are traded.

According to StoneX, Securitize management said during its second-quarter results call in August that most of its tokenization revenue came from integration fees. As a result, only a very small portion of the $5.3 billion in trading volume during the quarter generated revenue for the company.

The new platform is expected to change that picture. Securitize will now be able to generate revenue from trading and service fees; services related to collateral could also generate additional revenue in the future.

Securitize Stocks offers tokenized shares of companies including Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla on Solana. Trades are settled in USDC. These products are fully backed by the underlying shares and provide holders with dividend and shareholder rights.

StoneX forecasts that, driven by the new revenue model, the company’s revenue will reach approximately $120 million in 2027 and $198.5 million in 2028. That represents approximately 65% growth between the two years.

items.t: TRON Mainnet Voting Begins for 107 TVM Upgrade: TRX Price Rally Near?
sum: TRON's community is in the middle of a decision that could reshape how the network handles smart contracts, security, and computing costs. TRON Mainnet Voting for Committee Proposal No. 107 went live on August 25, 2026, and it is already drawing attention from developers and TRX holders alike.
The proposal is not a small tweak. It brings TRON up to speed with Ethereum's Prague and Osaka feature sets, and if it passes, the upgrade is set to activate on August 28 at 14:00 SGT.
TRON Mainnet Voting for Proposal 107 started on August 25, 2026, with an effective date targeted for August 28, 2026, per DAO's official X post.
The upgrade adds historical block hash queries, the CLZ opcode, native secp256r1 support for Passkey verification, and lower MODEXP energy costs.
TRX trades at $0.3427 with a $32.528 billion market cap, sitting about 20% below its all-time high of $0.4313, according to CoinGecko data.

Proposal 107 brings TRON's virtual machine, the TVM, in line with Ethereum's Prague and Osaka upgrades, both bundled into TRON's own GreatVoyage-v4.8.2 release, nicknamed Pyrrho. In plain terms, the TVM is the engine that runs every smart contract it, so an upgrade here touches every app built on the chain.

Four changes stand out. Historical block hash queries let smart contracts look back at older block data without extra workarounds. The CLZ opcode speeds up certain math operations used in contract code.

Bitcoin Back at $65,000 as Oil and Gas Prices Fall
sum: The U.S. and Iran have held fire for a second consecutive day, and risk appetite is returning to the markets. Bitcoin is back above $65,000, while Ethereum is climbing considerably faster — fuelling hopes of an emerging rotation into altcoins.

It is a pattern familiar from recent months: as soon as the guns fall silent in the Middle East, sentiment on financial markets turns. After the United States and Iran refrained from airstrikes for a second day running on Sunday, the classic “peace trades” are back. Oil prices are dropping sharply, equity futures are gaining — and crypto assets are riding along.

Bitcoin has reclaimed the $65,000 mark and is trading at around $65,500. Ether is back at nearly $1,965, making it the clear outperformer among the large-cap assets. Solana, XRP and the remaining top-10 tokens are also in the green.

The energy market is showing the sharpest reaction. WTI futures gapped lower on Monday and are down around five percent at roughly $85. Brent crude is falling 4.7 percent to $92.19. Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures are each up around half a percent, while on currency markets the Australian dollar and the euro are gaining against the greenback — a textbook risk-on picture.

The war, which began in late February, had already given way once to a fragile ceasefire in the second quarter, only for it to unravel quickly. Iran has now reportedly signalled that it will keep airstrikes suspended for as long as the U.S. does the same. Whether that turns into a durable peace process remains an open question — but markets are certainly pricing in the possibility.

What Is TRC-20? How TRC-20 Tokens Work on TRON
sum: Sending crypto should be simple. Yet one wrong network choice can freeze your funds, delay a payment, or send tokens where you can’t recover them.

That’s why it’s important to know how USDT-TRC20, TRON addresses, TRX fees, and token standards work. So before you move money on TRON, you need to know what TRC-20 means, how it works, and what to check before every transfer. Keep reading for all the information in one convenient place.

TRC-20 is a token standard on the TRON blockchain. It defines the rules smart contracts must follow to create fungible tokens. It works similarly to ERC-20 on the Ethereum blockchain, but it runs on TRON instead of the Ethereum network.

In practical terms, a TRC-20 token is a smart contract deployed on the TRON network. That contract runs inside the TRON Virtual Machine, TRON’s smart contract runtime. The TVM executes blockchain code and helps keep token issuance, transfers, and burns consistent across wallets, exchanges, and dApps.
TRC-20 supports many token types, including utility tokens, security tokens, and stablecoins such as USDT issued on the TRON blockchain.

TRC-20 is the main technical standard for fungible tokens issued on TRON. It serves a similar role to ERC-20 on Ethereum by standardizing how platforms read balances, process transfers, and detect token activity.

TRON promotes itself as a high-speed, low-cost blockchain for moving value at scale. The TRC-20 standard supports that positioning because it helps wallets, exchanges, payment apps, and other platforms integrate TRON-based assets more easily.

items.t: CPI Confirms Cooling Trend but Offers No Green Light for Rate Cuts
sum: The latest U.S. inflation data passed through markets with little drama, reinforcing the view that price pressures are easing at a measured pace rather than collapsing outright.
With no upside shock in the numbers, investors quickly shifted focus from the headline figure to what it implies for interest rates, liquidity, and risk appetite going forward.

The CPI report confirmed a familiar pattern. Overall inflation stayed unchanged on an annual basis, while core inflation dipped slightly to 2.6%. That combination suggests progress, but not enough to signal a decisive break from elevated price levels. Consumers continue to feel pressure from everyday costs, even as some categories show relief.

Housing costs once again played an outsized role, with shelter prices posting solid monthly gains. Food prices climbed sharply, and energy prices moved modestly higher, offsetting declines in areas such as used vehicles and household goods. The uneven mix explains why inflation is cooling slowly rather than falling rapidly.

For the Federal Reserve, the data supports patience. Inflation is no longer accelerating, but it remains above the 2% target. Markets still expect rates to move lower eventually, driven in part by signs of softening in the labor market, yet pricing continues to reflect limited confidence in an imminent cut.

Market reactions reflected that balance. Equities typically welcome inflation that does not surprise to the upside, but without a clear disinflationary trend, upside momentum remains constrained. Crypto markets tend to respond similarly: stable inflation helps preserve liquidity conditions, but without a clear signal that policy easing is close, major digital assets may remain range-bound.

The next potential catalyst is the Producer Price Index, scheduled for release on Wednesday. Because it tracks inflation earlier in the supply chain, PPI can influence expectations for future consumer prices. A hotter reading could revive concerns over sticky inflation, while a cooler print would strengthen the case for rate cuts later on.

items.t: Tether freezes $182 million in USDT stablecoin across five Tron blockchain wallets
sum: The freezes were part of Tether's policy to comply with U.S. Treasury sanctions and were executed in a coordinated manner.
- Tether froze over $182 million in USDT across five wallets on the Tron blockchain, according to onchain data tracked by Whale Alert.
- The wallet freezes, one of the largest in recent months, were part of Tether's policy to comply with U.S. Treasury sanctions and executed in a coordinated manner.
- USDT is the leading stablecoin, with over $187 billion in circulation, representing about 64% of the global stablecoin market.

Tether froze more than $182 million worth of its USDT stablecoin across five wallet addresses on the Tron blockchain on Jan. 11, according to onchain data tracked by Whale Alert, one of the larger single-day enforcement actions disclosed on Tron in recent months.
The wallets each held between roughly $12 million and $50 million in USDT. The freezes were executed within the same day, suggesting a coordinated action rather than a series of unrelated incidents.
The move aligns with Tether’s voluntary wallet-freezing policy, which it formalized in late 2023 to comply with the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions framework.

items.t: Kalshi adds TRON support, expanding access to onchain liquidity.

TRON joins Kalshi’s growing list of supported blockchain ecosystems, furthering our commitment to building the most accessible and efficient infrastructure for real-world event trading.
